Proof 1: Riesz representation: continuous linear functional on Hilbert space H has form f(x) =

Statement: Riesz representation: continuous linear functional on Hilbert space H has form f(x) =

Hypotheses: H Hilbert space, f: H -> F continuous linear

Conclusion: exists unique y in H with f(x) =

Definitions: continuous linear functional, Riesz, inner product

Proof (Variation #1):

Step 1: If f=0, take y=0

Step 2: Otherwise let N = ker(f), closed subspace

Step 3: H = N + N^perp (orthogonal decomposition)

Step 4: Choose z in N^perp with f(z)=1

Step 5: Define y = conj(f(z))/||z||^2 * z

Step 6: Show f(x) = for all x

ID: 119b95e81d4c | Status: UNFORMALIZED | Complexity: O(n)

Mutation test: Removing 'Hilbert': L^1 dual is L^infinity, not isometric

Provenance: Variation #1 for theorem in domain Functional_Analysis

Proof 2: Banach fixed point: contraction on complete metric space has unique fixed point

Statement: Banach fixed point: contraction on complete metric space has unique fixed point

Hypotheses: (M,d) complete metric space, T: M -> M contraction (Lipschitz L<1)

Conclusion: unique x* with T(x*) = x*

Definitions: contraction, complete metric, fixed point

Proof (Variation #2):

Step 1: Choose any x_0, define x_{n+1} = T(x_n)

Step 2: d(x_{n+1}, x_n) <= L * d(x_n, x_{n-1})

Step 3: d(x_n, x_m) <= L^m * d(x_0,x_1)/(1-L) -> 0

Step 4: (x_n) Cauchy, converges to x* by completeness

Step 5: T(x*) = T(lim x_n) = lim T(x_n) = lim x_{n+1} = x*

Step 6: Uniqueness: if T(y*)=y*, d(x*,y*) <= L*d(x*,y*), so d=0

ID: c71dc261d967 | Status: UNFORMALIZED | Complexity: O(n^2)

Mutation test: Removing 'complete': Q with T(x)=x/2 has no fixed point in Q

Provenance: Variation #2 for theorem in domain Functional_Analysis

Conclusion: unique x* with T(x*) = x*

Definitions: contraction, complete metric, fixed point

Proof (Variation #988):

Step 4: (x_n) Cauchy, converges to x* by completeness

Step 5: T(x*) = T(lim x_n) = lim T(x_n) = lim x_{n+1} = x*

Step 6: Uniqueness: if T(y*)=y*, d(x*,y*) <= L*d(x*,y*), so d=0

Step 2: At each step, bound functional by norm

Step 3: Use Zorn's lemma for infinite-dimensional case

Step 4: Norm preservation by construction

Proof 3: Closed graph theorem: T: X->Y has closed graph iff T is bounded (X,Y Banach)

Statement: Closed graph theorem: T: X->Y has closed graph iff T is bounded (X,Y Banach)

Hypotheses: X,Y Banach, T: X->Y linear

Conclusion: T bounded <=> graph closed

Definitions: closed graph, bounded, Banach

Proof:

Step 1: Define Gamma: X -> X x Y by x -> (x, Tx)

Step 2: If graph closed, Gamma is closed operator

Step 3: X x Y Banach, Gamma bijective onto closed subspace

Step 4: By open mapping theorem, Gamma^{-1} bounded

Step 5: Therefore T = proj_2 o Gamma^{-1} bounded

Proof 4: Uniform boundedness principle: pointwise bounded family on Banach space is uniformly bounded

Statement: Uniform boundedness principle: pointwise bounded family on Banach space is uniformly bounded

Hypotheses: X Banach, {T_alpha} bounded linear, sup_alpha ||T_alpha x|| < inf for each x

Conclusion: sup_alpha ||T_alpha|| < infinity

Definitions: uniform boundedness, Banach, pointwise

Proof:

Step 1: Define F_n = {x : sup_alpha ||T_alpha x|| <= n}

Step 2: F_n closed, union is X

Step 3: By Baire category: some F_N has interior

Step 4: Ball in F_N gives uniform bound
